newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mixed after directionless session.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mixed after directionless session.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled mixed after what traders said was a slow, directionless session.

"Our trade today was quite typical of the trade over the last three sessions in which we open lower but attempt to close near our day's highs. What caused us to refrain today was a little jockeying from professional players who are maybe still a bit bearish," a Kansas City broker said.
Wheat opened lower but firmed early amid fund-related buying. Added support came from the potential for more sales of U.S. wheat to Pakistan and Egypt.
But pressure came from signs the market remained technically overbought, traders said. Values were also undermined by hedging tied to ongoing active farmer sales at country elevators.
As it did several times this week, wheat played a following role Friday to CBOT corn and soybeans, which flip-flopped amid conflicting forecasts for weather next week in the Corn Belt.
"The market is probably going to be lackluster until we get a better idea about weather because of its direct impact on corn and beans and its indirect impact on wheat," a trader said.
KCBT wheat settled 2-1/2 cents per bushel lower to one cent higher, with Sept up 1/4 cent at $3.67-1/2. Earlier, Sept had been up as much as 3-3/4 cents at $3.71.

Traders said Wolcott Lincoln bought five million September bushels on the day. Farmland and Farmers Commodities each sold one million Sept, and FIMAT sold 1.5 million Sept and 1.4 million December bushels.
Volume was estimated at 33.5 million bushels, down from 38.965 million bushels Thursday.
